Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass only if the jacket's front panels are visibly brought together across the closure, with no visible gap along the closure. Fail only if the front closure is directly visible and a gap between the panels is clearly discernible. Do not treat fabric displaced or flared by pose or motion as proof of an opening. Unknown if the closure cannot be assessed directly or the panels' relationship is obscured; do not infer edited closure from the source image.
node.binding: Identify the same jacket using the source image, then inspect its front closure in the edited image. Base the decision on directly visible panel edges and closure, distinguishing a genuine gap from fabric displaced by pose or motion. The source is for garment identification only, not evidence of edited closure.

node_traces.evidence: The same pink jacket is identifiable, but in the edited image she is turned sideways and the front closure and relationship between the panels are obscured. The flared fabric could be due to her pose or motion, so it does not establish whether the jacket is open or fully closed.

d1-progress: The node is appropriately cautious about pose and fabric flare, but its binding makes comparable front-panel edges and opening width the only usable evidence. In these images the source shows a mostly frontal view with a visible dark center opening, while the edit turns the woman sideways and the jacket swings outward; that prevents a reliable width comparison, but does not by itself establish either progress or absence of progress. Keep this check limited to partial movement toward closure, and clarify how to assess any other directly visible, comparable evidence of the same jacket’s closure state without treating pose, flare, or motion as progress. If no such evidence is discernible, retain unknown rather than forcing a label. The trace is valid and queried with no dependency or transport failure, so this is an evidence/criterion robustness issue, not an execution failure. The aggregate reference label is not atomic ground truth and does not justify changing the criterion to force yes; investigate why the requested edit is unresolved under this view.
